items.action: Patch internet-facing PHP immediately and forensically triage exposed systems for webshells or persistence; systems that cannot be updated should be taken offline.
items.details: The flaws are CVE-2026-109618 (memory corruption) and CVE-2026-109619 (stale internal request state), both rated CVSS 9.2 and allowing unauthenticated remote code execution. Fixed in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. PHP powers roughly 70% of websites, per CIO Dive.
items.summary: Researchers at Perplexity detected the first successful exploitation of the critical PHP2Shell flaws, achieving remote code execution against a honeypot running PHP 8.4.26 under Apache mod_php. CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Oct 26, with a federal remediation deadline of Oct 29.
items.title: PHP2Shell exploitation confirmed; federal patch deadline is today

items.action: Update Node.js, Brotli libraries and every product bundling them, and hunt for exploitation attempts against internet-facing services that decode Brotli data.
items.details: The out-of-bounds write affects Brotli 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 and can crash applications, disclose memory, or allow remote code execution via crafted compressed data. Fixes shipped Oct 21 in Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1, plus Brotli 1.0.10, 1.1.1 and 1.2.1. Broadcom warned on Oct 27 that VMware SDDC Manager is affected and patches are pending, with workarounds published.
items.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-111497, the critical Brotli decoder flaw known as Node2Shell, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Oct 27, with a federal remediation deadline of Nov 10. Two security firms recorded exploitation attempts against honeypots on Oct 26-27.
items.title: Node2Shell (Brotli) added to CISA KEV as honeypots log exploitation attempts

items.action: Apply the fixed ASA/FTD releases, or disable secondary authentication on affected tunnel groups as an interim mitigation.
items.details: The flaw stems from logic errors when secondary authentication is configured on a tunnel group, and no successful VPN login is required. It affects ASA 9.16-9.24 and FTD 7.0-10.1 in that configuration. Cisco says there are no workarounds, but disabling secondary authentication on affected tunnel groups mitigates it until patching.
items.summary: Cisco disclosed CVE-2026-76418 (CVSS 8.6) on Oct 28 in ASA and Firepower Threat Defense software, and said its PSIRT became aware of active exploitation in October 2026. An unauthenticated attacker can send a crafted SSL VPN request and force the device to reload, causing denial of service.
items.title: Cisco Secure Firewall SSL VPN flaw actively exploited to force device reloads

items.action: Treat the listing as an early warning signal: verify credentials, mailboxes and document systems, and review exposure if the firm is a client or counterparty.
items.details: SilentRansomGroup typically follows a double-extortion model, exfiltrating data before encryption. The group also listed fellow law firm Morrison Cohen on Oct 26. Law firms are high-value targets because of the sensitive client material they hold.
items.summary: International law firm Morrison Foerster was listed by the SilentRansomGroup ransomware group on its leak site on Oct 28, 2026, according to ransomware-tracking feeds. The listing is a claim only; no encryption, data theft or operational impact has been confirmed in public reporting.
items.title: SilentRansomGroup lists law firm Morrison Foerster on leak site (claim)

items.action: Monitor for data publication and credential exposure; anyone connected to the firm should watch for identity-theft and phishing attempts using the claimed data.
items.details: The claim has not been independently confirmed. Akira is one of the most active ransomware groups, and listings of this kind are commonly used to pressure victims before data is published.
items.summary: The Akira ransomware group listed Roberts Consulting Services, a US engineering and construction-materials testing firm, on Oct 28. The listing says it will upload 28GB of corporate data, including detailed employee information such as passport scans, driving licences and Social Security numbers, plus contracts, client information and financials.
items.title: Akira claims Roberts Consulting Services, threatens 28GB data release

items.action: Treat any email about this breach containing a link as a red flag — Bandai Namco says its genuine notices will not contain URLs — and stay alert for phishing using the exposed addresses.
items.details: YmirLink's wider leak grew to more than 51.62 million records, mostly email addresses, according to NHK reporting cited by Times of India, affecting other organisations including Japanese railway operators. Bandai Namco suspended the email service and reported the incident to Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission.
items.summary: Bandai Namco confirmed on Oct 28 that about 346,000 members of its GUNDAM base service had email addresses and internal ID numbers exposed after its email distribution provider, YmirLink, was compromised. Passwords, card details, names, addresses and purchase history were not leaked, the company said.
items.title: Bandai Namco confirms breach of ~346,000 users via third-party email provider

items.action: Smaller NBFCs and fintechs should urgently review payment-gateway and partner-bank API keys, whitelisted servers and disbursal controls, and warn customers about AI-scripted phishing calls.
items.details: Investigators found the Chinese hacking platform CyberStrike in the few completed probes, and experts cited a combination of AI toolkits Artex and CyberStrike alongside Chinese open-source models. CERT-In has warned the frameworks cut the time from break-in to damage from days to hours and told organisations to prioritise alerts on ARTEX and CyberStrike. One Delhi NBFC lost ₹7.5 crore and then a further ₹7.25 crore days later.
items.summary: About ₹300 crore is estimated to have been siphoned from mostly smaller non-banking financial companies across India in cyberattacks over the past two months, with nearly 150 complaints or FIRs filed, sources told The Economic Times. Attackers studied payment patterns for 10-12 days before striking, in some cases hitting the same NBFC twice.
items.title: AI-driven cyberattacks siphon an estimated ₹300 crore from small NBFCs in two months

items.action: Revoke keys at the provider first, then delete and replace them in Rocket; check provider usage and billing from Oct 27 onward for unrecognised activity.
items.details: Unauthorised access ran for about five and a half hours, from 6:32 PM to 11:58 PM UTC on Oct 27. Rocket says it identified and fixed the root cause and the attacker no longer has access. It has not said how the attacker got in, whether decryption keys were also reached, or how many accounts 0.2% represents — roughly 3,000 if its April figure of 1.5 million users still holds, though Cyber Kendra notes that is only an estimate.
items.summary: Rocket.new, the Surat-based AI app-building platform, told users an attacker broke into part of its production systems on Oct 27 and obtained the encrypted API keys of about 0.2% of its users. In a notification sent Oct 28, it asked every user to revoke and replace third-party keys connected to Rocket, even if their keys were not in the compromised set.
items.title: Surat-based Rocket.new says attacker obtained encrypted API keys of 0.2% of users

items.action: Use the PHP incident as a prompt to audit patching, breach-notification and data-protection safeguards against DPDP requirements ahead of the May 2027 deadline.
items.details: Experts say the incidents underline the need to identify gaps in companies' security practices and clarify what counts as reasonable safeguards before the law takes full effect.
items.summary: Legal and policy experts have called for targeted assessments of corporate readiness for India's Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act following recent cyber incidents in India, including the disclosure of critical PHP vulnerabilities. The Act is being implemented in phases, with a May 2027 deadline for full compliance obligations.
items.title: PHP scare prompts calls for urgent DPDP readiness audits in India
